title: Dephasing-Enhanced Response and Phase Transitions in Quantum Boltzmann Samplers
authors: Yu-Xuan Zhang, Jing-Ling Chen, Leong-Chuan Kwek, Peng Wang
abstract: Dephasing can drive a quantum Boltzmann sampler into an ordered phase while its programmed probability distribution remains disordered. We trace this transition to an enhanced conditional response: coherence loss changes how each spin responds to its neighbors, and interactions amplify the change. For all-to-all coupling, we establish the stationary transition at finite dephasing. Near criticality, the magnetization distribution depends on the ratio of dephasing strength to the square root of system size, retaining a finite imprint of coherence even as the local coherent correction vanishes. In the strong-dephasing limit on a square lattice, the dynamics generates effective multispin interactions and probability currents, with Ising-like critical statistics. Adjusting the local dissipative update restores the target probability process on arbitrary graphs.
summary: This work analyzes quantum Boltzmann samplers to understand how environmental dephasing drives the system into ordered phases, even when the desired target distribution is disordered. By analyzing the master equation and critical fluctuations, the authors establish a finite transition point and derive the scaling behavior of the magnetization near criticality. This shows that quantum noise can fundamentally alter the phase transition landscape of complex interacting quantum systems.
main_problem: The paper investigates how dephasing affects the response and phase transitions in quantum Boltzmann samplers, especially when the underlying target probability distribution is disordered.
main_result: Dephasing can drive the quantum sampler into an ordered phase even if the target distribution is disordered, and the critical fluctuations retain a finite imprint of coherence.
method: The analysis involves deriving and solving the master equation governing the density matrix evolution, linearizing around fixed points, and using scaling arguments near criticality.
model_or_system: The system is a quantum Boltzmann sampler modeled by interacting spins ($\sigma_i = \pm 1$) whose dynamics are governed by a master equation incorporating engineered dissipative updates and phase noise ($\gamma$).

paper_structure: The paper progresses by establishing the dynamics via a master equation, analyzing local and collective responses, determining the critical thresholds, and finally deriving the stationary law for the rescaled magnetization in the critical limit.
why_interesting: The study provides a concrete, quantum-mechanical framework for understanding how noise (dephasing) can induce order or drive phase transitions in complex many-body systems, linking quantum dynamics to classical critical phenomena.
